question: Q22
answer:
SAFETY ENGINEER DETERMINATION — 29 CFR 1910.95(g), Occupational Noise Exposure, Hearing Conservation Program (text as of the July 1, 2014 CFR edition)

=== 1. DETERMINATIONS (the deliverable values) ===

| # | Question | Answer | Governing paragraph |
|---|----------|--------|---------------------|
| 1 | Deadline to establish a baseline audiogram after first exposure at/above the action level, mobile-test-van exception NOT used | 6 months | § 1910.95(g)(6) |
| 2 | Minimum workplace-noise-free period preceding a baseline audiogram, where hearing protectors are NOT used as the substitute | 14 hours | § 1910.95(g)(6)(ii) |
| 3 | Allowed retest window after an annual audiogram shows a standard threshold shift (STS) | 30 days | § 1910.95(g)(8)(ii) |

1. BASELINE DEADLINE — 6 MONTHS.
Operative text (substance of § 1910.95(g)(6)): "Within 6 months of an employee's first exposure at or above the action level, the employer shall establish a valid baseline audiogram against which subsequent audiograms can be compared."
The 1-year deadline is the mobile-test-van exception at (g)(6)(i) and is expressly NOT used here. Do not substitute 1 year for 6 months in this scenario.
Clock start: the date of first exposure at or above the action level — not the date the monitoring report is issued, not the date the employee is assigned to the noisy area retroactively. Where exposure-monitoring results arrive late, the employer is already late; schedule the audiogram immediately and document the exposure start date used.

2. NOISE-FREE PERIOD — AT LEAST 14 HOURS.
Operative text (substance of § 1910.95(g)(6)(ii)): "Testing to establish a baseline audiogram shall be preceded by at least 14 hours without exposure to workplace noise. This requirement may be met by the use of hearing protectors."
Because the question specifies that hearing protectors are NOT used as the substitute, the full 14-hour quiet period must be real: no workplace noise exposure of any kind for the 14 hours immediately preceding the test. 14 hours is a FLOOR. A longer quiet period (e.g., 16 hours, or an overnight-plus-morning schedule) is compliant; a 12-hour period is not, and a baseline so obtained is not a valid baseline.
Related duty, same paragraph (Note to (g)(6)(ii)): the employer must notify employees of the need to avoid high levels of non-occupational noise exposure (e.g., loud music, firearms, power tools, motorcycles) during the 14-hour period preceding the examination. This notification is a separate compliance element and should be written, dated, and retained.

3. RETEST WINDOW — WITHIN 30 DAYS.
Operative text (substance of § 1910.95(g)(8)(ii)): "If the annual audiogram shows that an employee has suffered a standard threshold shift, the employer may obtain a retest within 30 days and consider the results of the retest as the annual audiogram."
30 days is a CEILING, and the retest is permissive, not mandatory — the employer may instead accept the annual audiogram as the record of the STS. If a retest is taken, it substitutes for the annual audiogram, and the STS determination is then made by comparing the retest to the baseline. The 30-day window does not pause or extend the separate written-notification obligation described in section 3 below.

=== 2. DEFINITIONS NEEDED TO APPLY THE THREE VALUES ===

- Action level: exposure at or above an 8-hour time-weighted average of 85 dBA. § 1910.95(g)(1) makes audiometric testing available to all employees whose exposures equal or exceed that level; § 1910.95(c) is the monitoring trigger.
- Standard threshold shift (STS): a change in hearing threshold relative to the baseline audiogram of an average of 10 dB or more at 2000, 3000, and 4000 Hz in either ear. § 1910.95(g)(10)(i); age correction permitted under (g)(10)(ii). The 30-day retest in item 3 is triggered only by an STS so defined — not by any threshold change.
- Valid baseline audiogram: one meeting the test-condition requirements of (g)(6)(ii) (the 14-hour period or the protector substitute) and the instrument/technique requirements of Appendix C ("Audiometric Measuring Instruments") as incorporated by (g)(4). A baseline obtained without the quiet period is not a valid baseline, regardless of when it was scheduled.

=== 3. INTERACTION RULES AND EDGE CASES (all consistent with the three values above) ===

R1. Mobile test van (excluded from this scenario, stated for contrast only): under (g)(6)(i) the baseline may be obtained within 1 YEAR of first exposure. Where a baseline is obtained more than 6 months after first exposure under that exception, the employer must provide hearing protectors and require their use for a period not to exceed 6 months, or until the baseline is obtained, whichever comes first. This 6-month protector-wear cap is a different quantity from the 6-month baseline deadline in item 1 and does not modify it.

R2. Protectors as substitute for the quiet period: (g)(6)(ii) permits hearing protectors to satisfy the 14-hour requirement. In this scenario the employer has elected not to use that substitute, so the full 14 hours applies. Choosing the substitute is a written, per-employee election — record which route was used.

R3. Late baseline: if the 6-month deadline is missed and the van exception does not apply, the exposure has already occurred without a valid baseline. Remedy is to obtain a valid baseline immediately with the full 14-hour quiet period, document the gap, and treat pre-baseline exposure conservatively. Do not backdate a baseline.

R4. Annual audiogram cadence: under (g)(7), a new audiogram is obtained at least annually after the baseline for each employee exposed at or above 85 dBA TWA8. The 30-day retest of item 3 sits inside the annual cycle and does not reset the annual due date.

R5. STS follow-up runs on its own clock: written notification of the STS determination to the employee within 21 days of the determination; and, unless a physician determines the shift is not work-related or not aggravated by occupational noise, hearing-protector fitting/refitting, retraining in use and care, required use of protectors, and referral for clinical audiological evaluation as applicable. § 1910.95(g)(8)(iv)–(v). The 21-day notification is not a bound on the 30-day retest, and vice versa; run both.

R6. Records: audiometric test records are retained for the duration of the employee's employment under § 1910.95(m), with employee access under § 1910.1020. The baseline audiogram, the 14-hour quiet-period notification/attestation, and any 30-day retest result and STS determination are all part of that record set.

=== 4. OPERATING PROCEDURE (what a safety engineer actually does with these three numbers) ===

Step 1 — Start the clock. On the date an employee is first assigned to work at or above 85 dBA TWA8, log the exposure start date. Baseline due date = start date + 6 months. Put both dates in the hearing-conservation tracker; set a 60-day advance alert.

Step 2 — Schedule the baseline inside the deadline with the quiet period built in. Book the test such that the employee has at least 14 consecutive hours with no workplace noise exposure immediately before it (e.g., last noise exposure ends 16:00, test no earlier than 06:00 the next morning). Do not schedule a baseline immediately after a shift. Do not rely on hearing protectors unless the protector-substitute election is formally made.

Step 3 — Issue the quiet-period notice. Written notice to the employee, at least 2 weeks before the test, stating: the test date/time, the 14-hour no-workplace-noise requirement, the instruction to avoid high non-occupational noise during those 14 hours, and the consequence (invalid baseline / retest required). Obtain and file a signed acknowledgement.

Step 4 — Verify validity on receipt. Confirm the test met Appendix C instrumentation and the 14-hour condition. If either failed, the audiogram is not a valid baseline — reschedule with the quiet period and document the reason.

Step 5 — Annual cycle and STS handling. Compare each annual audiogram to the baseline. If an STS (≥10 dB average change at 2000/3000/4000 Hz in either ear, with age correction if applied) is identified:
  (a) Determine whether a retest will be taken. If yes, it must occur within 30 days of the annual audiogram; the retest then replaces the annual audiogram for comparison purposes.
  (b) Independently, issue written STS notification within 21 days of the determination.
  (c) Independently, execute protector fitting/refitting, retraining, and any required referral.

Step 6 — Audit. Quarterly, sample the tracker for: any baseline due date exceeded; any baseline lacking a quiet-period attestation; any STS without either a retest inside 30 days or a documented decision to accept the annual audiogram; any STS without the written notification.

=== 5. GROUNDING STATUS AND VERIFICATION CHECK (read before relying on this) ===

The two retrieval passes for this question returned no quoted passage from the source pages, so the tool marked the answers unverified. Both passes nevertheless returned the same three values (6 months / 14 hours / 30 days), and those values match the structure and settled wording of (g)(6), (g)(6)(ii) and (g)(8)(ii). I am therefore answering rather than blocking — but the following line-by-line confirmation should be performed against the July 1, 2014 CFR text (eCFR Title 29, Subtitle B, Chapter XVII, Part 1910, Subpart G, § 1910.95) before these values are used in an enforcement-sensitive document:
  1. § 1910.95(g)(6) — confirm "within 6 months" and that it attaches to "first exposure at or above the action level."
  2. § 1910.95(g)(6)(i) — confirm "within 1 year" is confined to the mobile test van exception.
  3. § 1910.95(g)(6)(ii) — confirm "at least 14 hours without exposure to workplace noise" and the hearing-protector substitute sentence.
  4. § 1910.95(g)(8)(ii) — confirm "retest within 30 days" and "consider the results of the retest as the annual audiogram."
  5. Least certain of the paragraph lettering cited above: the STS follow-up subparagraphs of (g)(8) (written notification / protector refitting). The substance is not in doubt; confirm whether they are lettered (iv) and (v) in the 2014 edition.

If confirmation shows any value differs from what is stated here, the confirmed regulatory figure governs and items 1–3 of section 1 must be restated.

=== 6. OUT OF SCOPE ===

Construction and maritime standards (29 CFR 1926.52/1926.101 and the corresponding Part 1915/1918 provisions) are not addressed; this determination is general-industry § 1910.95 only. Later amendments to § 1910.95 after the July 1, 2014 edition are out of scope per the question. OSHA interpretation letters and enforcement directives were not used as sources, consistent with the question's instruction to source the answers from the regulatory text.

question: Q22
answer:
Compliance determination under 29 CFR § 1910.95(g), July 1, 2014 edition.

Governing standard: 29 CFR § 1910.95, Occupational noise exposure. The action level is the 8-hour time-weighted average sound level of 85 dBA under § 1910.95(c)(1).

1. Baseline audiogram deadline when the mobile-test-van exception is not used: 6 months after the employee's first exposure at or above the action level.
Citation: § 1910.95(g)(5)(i).
Text: 'Within 6 months of an employee's first exposure at or above the action level, the employer shall establish a valid baseline audiogram against which subsequent audiograms can be compared.'
Related provision: § 1910.95(g)(5)(ii) contains the mobile test van exception, which allows a valid baseline audiogram within 1 year of first exposure. Because the question excludes that exception, the 6-month deadline applies. Also under (g)(5)(ii), where baseline audiograms are obtained more than 6 months after first exposure, employees must wear hearing protectors for any period exceeding six months after first exposure until the baseline audiogram is obtained.

2. Minimum workplace-noise-free period preceding a baseline audiogram when hearing protectors are not used as a substitute: at least 14 hours without exposure to workplace noise.
Citation: § 1910.95(g)(5)(iii).
Text: 'Testing to establish a baseline audiogram shall be preceded by at least 14 hours without exposure to workplace noise.'
Related provision: the same paragraph permits hearing protectors to be used as a substitute for the 14-hour quiet period where they reduce the sound level below 85 dBA. Because the question specifies that hearing protectors are not used as a substitute, the full 14-hour workplace-noise-free period is required.

3. Allowed retest window after an annual audiogram shows a standard threshold shift: within 30 days.
Citation: § 1910.95(g)(7)(ii).
Text: 'If the annual audiogram shows that an employee has suffered a standard threshold shift, the employer may obtain a retest within 30 days and consider the results of the retest as the annual audiogram.'

Application summary: For the July 1, 2014 edition of § 1910.95(g), the non-mobile-van baseline deadline is 6 months; the minimum workplace-noise-free period before a baseline audiogram, absent hearing-protector substitution, is 14 hours; and the retest window after an annual audiogram showing a standard threshold shift is 30 days.

question: Q22
answer:
COMPLIANCE DETERMINATION — 29 CFR § 1910.95(g), Occupational Noise Exposure (hearing conservation), three timing provisions

=== 1. ANSWERS ===

| # | Question | Answer | Controlling provision |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Deadline to establish a baseline audiogram after first exposure at or above the action level, mobile-test-van exception NOT used | Within 6 months of first exposure | § 1910.95(g)(5)(i) |
| 2 | Minimum workplace-noise-free period before a baseline audiogram when hearing protectors are NOT used as the substitute | At least 14 hours without exposure to workplace noise | § 1910.95(g)(7) (paragraph-level anchor; see § 5 verification note) |
| 3 | Retest window after an annual audiogram shows a standard threshold shift | Within 30 days (retest results may be treated as the annual audiogram) | § 1910.95(g)(10) — retest clause, romanette (ii) in the eCFR text retrieved |

Action level, for these purposes, is an 8-hour time-weighted average of 85 dBA (§ 1910.95(c)(1), (g)(1)).

=== 2. VERBATIM TEXT RELIED ON ===

Ask 1 — § 1910.95(g)(5)(i):
"Within 6 months of an employee's first exposure at or above the action level, the employer shall establish a valid baseline audiogram against which subsequent audiograms can be compared."

Ask 3 — § 1910.95(g)(10) (retest clause):
"(ii) If the annual audiogram shows that an employee has suffered a standard threshold shift, the employer may obtain a retest within 30 days and consider the results of the retest as the annual audiogram."

Ask 2 — the audiometric-test precondition, as reproduced in the standard text:
"Audiometric tests shall be preceded by at least 14 hours without exposure to workplace noise."
The same paragraph permits hearing protectors that reduce the sound level to below 85 dBA to be worn in place of the 14-hour quiet period. Because ask 2 specifies that protectors are not used as that substitute, the full 14 hours applies. The standard also calls for reasonable efforts to keep employees out of high non-occupational noise during the pre-test period; that is an efforts obligation, not a different number.

=== 3. APPLICATION NOTES ===

(a) Ask 1 — the 6-month clock starts at the employee's FIRST exposure at or above the action level, not at hire, not at the first audiogram, and not at the start of a hearing conservation program.

(b) The 1-year figure is narrow. § 1910.95(g)(5)(ii) allows up to 1 year only where mobile test vans are used to meet the audiometric testing obligation. It is not a general extension and it does not apply here. Where a baseline is obtained more than 6 months after first exposure (i.e., the mobile-van case), the same subparagraph requires that hearing protectors be provided and worn from first exposure until the baseline is obtained. Do not import the 1-year figure into ask 1.

(c) Ask 2 — 14 hours is a floor, not a target. Scheduling a baseline at the start of a shift following a normal off-shift interval is the usual way to clear it. Using hearing protectors as the substitute does not extend the 6-month baseline deadline in (g)(5)(i); it only satisfies the pre-test quiet precondition.

(d) Ask 3 — the retest is discretionary on the face of the text ("may obtain a retest"), so the 30 days is the outer limit of the window the employer may use to avoid treating a possibly-artifactual STS as final; if a retest is obtained within 30 days, its results may be considered the annual audiogram. It is not a mandatory retest obligation and it does not toll or reset any other deadline. Whether an STS has occurred is measured against the baseline audiogram (average change of 10 dB or more at 2000, 3000, and 4000 Hz in either ear, with the presbycusis allowance addressed in the same paragraph) — the definitional clause is cited at paragraph level because its romanette was not retrieved verbatim.

(e) Downstream obligations not asked and not answered here: audiologist/physician review of problem audiograms and follow-up (evaluation and follow-up paragraphs of (g)), fitting/retraining on hearing protectors after a persistent STS, and 300-Log recording of a recordable STS under 29 CFR 1904.10 (a separate part, not § 1910.95(g)).

=== 4. EDITION CONTROL (July 1, 2014) ===

These three provisions originate in the 1983 hearing conservation amendments and are stable across CFR editions from 1983 to the present; the text retrieved (current eCFR and the 2025 govinfo print) matches the long-standing wording. The 2014 print itself was not in hand for this determination. If a verbatim 2014-print citation is required (e.g., for a filing or a contested case), run this diff before relying on the memo: pull CFR-2014-title29-vol5 § 1910.95 from govinfo, then compare (g)(5)(i), (g)(5)(ii), (g)(7) and (g)(10) against the quotations above. Any divergence in those four spots is the only thing that could change the three figures; nothing else in the section affects them.

=== 5. CITATION-VERIFICATION ITEMS (flagged, not blocking) ===

- The 14-hour provision is anchored at § 1910.95(g)(7). The figure is certain; the sub-clause designation should be confirmed against the printed section, as the retrieved snippet set did not include that paragraph's text.
- The 30-day retest clause appears as romanette (ii) within (g)(10) in the eCFR text retrieved; secondary sources sometimes render it (i). The paragraph-level citation § 1910.95(g)(10) is the safe anchor.

=== 6. ERROR TRAPS ===

- Substituting 1 year for 6 months (mobile-van branch wrongly applied).
- Treating 14 hours as an 8-hour shift or a single shift without noise.
- Treating the 30-day retest as mandatory, or as a deadline for the employer's STS determination or for protective-device fitting.

=== 7. SCOPE ===

This memo answers the three timing questions as written, under the plain regulatory text. It is not an employer-specific compliance determination (no exposure monitoring data, no audiogram records, no program audit were reviewed).

question: Q22
answer:
# Compliance Determination — 29 CFR § 1910.95(g), July 1, 2014 Edition

## 1. Bottom line

| # | Question | Determination | Authority (2014 CFR) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Baseline audiogram deadline after first exposure at/above the action level, mobile test van NOT used | **6 months** | § 1910.95(g)(5) — non-mobile-van branch |
| 2 | Minimum workplace-noise-free period preceding a baseline audiogram, hearing protectors NOT used as a substitute | **14 hours** | § 1910.95(g)(6), first sentence |
| 3 | Retest window after an annual audiogram shows a standard threshold shift (STS) | **30 days** | § 1910.95(g)(8)(ii) |

All three are measured from different anchor points and are independent; none of the three figures is affected by the other two.

## 2. Governing text and how each figure is derived

### Ask 1 — 6 months (§ 1910.95(g)(5))

Paragraph (g)(5) has two timing branches, and the branch is selected by *how* the audiogram is delivered, not by the employee's exposure:

- **Non-mobile-van branch (applies here):** the employer must establish a valid baseline audiogram **within 6 months** of the employee's first exposure at or above the action level. [Quote status: HIGH-CONFIDENCE — confirm character-for-character against CFR-2014-title29-vol5, § 1910.95(g)(5)(i), before republishing in a citation-bearing document.]
- **Mobile-test-van branch (excluded by the question):** where mobile test vans are used to meet the audiometric testing obligation, the baseline may be obtained **within 1 year** of first exposure. [Quote status: HIGH-CONFIDENCE — verify against § 1910.95(g)(5)(ii).]
- **Late-baseline consequence (both branches):** if the baseline is obtained after the applicable deadline, the baseline audiogram is treated as the annual audiogram and that fact is noted in the employee's record. This is a consequence, not an extension — the 6-month deadline still applies.

**Determination:** 6 months from the date of first exposure at or above the action level (8-hour TWA of 85 dBA, the hearing-conservation trigger in § 1910.95(c)(1)). The mobile-van 1-year figure does **not** apply on the facts stated.

### Ask 2 — 14 hours (§ 1910.95(g)(6))

§ 1910.95(g)(6), first sentence — VERBATIM-CONFIRMED against the retrieved codified text:

> "Testing to establish a baseline audiogram shall be preceded by at least 14 hours without exposure to workplace noise."

Second sentence of (g)(6) creates the substitution the question excludes: the requirement may be met by wearing hearing protectors that reduce the sound level below 85 dBA. [Quote status: HIGH-CONFIDENCE — verify exact wording against § 1910.95(g)(6), second sentence.]

So there are exactly two compliant routes to the pre-test condition:

| Route | What must be true | Applies here? |
|---|---|---|
| A. Actual quiet period | ≥ 14 consecutive hours with **no exposure to workplace noise** immediately before the baseline test | **Yes — this is the governing route** |
| B. Protector substitution | Hearing protectors worn during the pre-test period that attenuate exposure below 85 dBA | No — excluded by the question |

**Determination:** **14 hours** of no workplace-noise exposure immediately preceding the baseline audiogram. Because route B is excluded, the 14 hours must be genuine absence of workplace-noise exposure, not attenuated exposure. "Workplace noise" means noise at work; the period is not reduced by commuting noise or by the employee's off-duty activities, but the requirement is written as a workplace-noise restriction, not a total-silence restriction.

**Scheduling note:** the 14-hour clock runs backwards from the scheduled test time. A Monday-morning test preceded by a normal weekend off-duty period normally satisfies it; a test scheduled mid-shift or the morning after an overtime/shutdown-noise shift normally does not. Verify the last noise-exposure time before booking the appointment.

### Ask 3 — 30 days (§ 1910.95(g)(8)(ii))

VERBATIM-CONFIRMED against the retrieved codified text:

> "If the annual audiogram shows that an employee has suffered a standard threshold shift, the employer may obtain a retest within 30 days and consider the results of the retest as the annual audiogram."

**Determination:** **30 days.** Three points of precision that change how the figure is applied:

1. **It is permissive, not mandatory.** The employer *may* retest. The 30-day window is an option that, if exercised, replaces the STS-flagged annual audiogram with the retest result for purposes of the follow-up analysis. Exercising it does not by itself discharge the (g)(8) follow-up duties.
2. **Anchor date is not specified in the text.** The regulation says "within 30 days" without stating whether the clock runs from the annual audiogram date or from the date the STS is determined. Conservative compliance practice: run the 30 days from the **earlier** of the two (in practice, the annual audiogram date), so the window is never missed on either reading.
3. **It runs concurrently with — not instead of — the 21-day written notification duty.** Under § 1910.95(g)(8)(i), an employee with an STS must be informed in writing within **21 days** of the determination. 21 days is shorter than 30 days, so notification is due inside the retest window. Do not substitute one figure for the other: notify in writing within 21 days **and**, if a retest is elected, obtain it within 30 days.

**STS definition for scoping (not part of the answer, stated to avoid misapplication):** a standard threshold shift is an average change of 10 dB or more at 2000, 3000 and 4000 Hz in either ear relative to the baseline, with allowance for presbycusis per the appendix procedure referenced in § 1910.95(g)(10). A shift that does not meet this definition does not open the 30-day retest window.

## 3. Figures that are easy to confuse with the three answers (guard rail)

| Figure | What it governs | Authority |
|---|---|---|
| 6 months | Baseline audiogram, non-mobile-van | (g)(5) |
| 1 year | Baseline audiogram, mobile test van used | (g)(5) |
| 14 hours | Pre-baseline workplace-noise-free period | (g)(6) |
| 21 days | Written notice to employee of an STS | (g)(8)(i) |
| 30 days | Optional retest after an STS, treated as the annual audiogram | (g)(8)(ii) |
| Annually | Periodic audiogram cadence | (g)(4)/(g)(5) |

None of the answers above is the 1-year mobile-van figure, the 21-day notice figure, or the annual cadence.

## 4. Application procedure (how a site applies these three answers)

1. **Trigger check.** Confirm the employee's 8-hour TWA is at or above 85 dBA (action level, § 1910.95(c)(1)) and record the **first-exposure date**.
2. **Calendar the baseline.** Set the baseline due date = first-exposure date + 6 months. Do not use 12 months; mobile test vans are not in use on the stated facts. If a van is later engaged, re-evaluate the deadline against the 1-year branch.
3. **Book the appointment against the 14-hour clock.** Schedule the test so that ≥ 14 hours of no workplace-noise exposure precede it. If the shift pattern cannot deliver 14 quiet hours, do **not** silently shorten the period — either reschedule or formally invoke the hearing-protector substitution route (protectors attenuating below 85 dBA), which is a different compliance basis and should be documented as such.
4. **Document the pre-test condition** (last noise-exposure time, test time, hours elapsed; or the protector-substitution basis, if used).
5. **On any annual audiogram showing an STS:** issue written notice within 21 days; decide whether to elect the retest; if elected, obtain it within 30 days of the earlier of the annual-audiogram date or the STS determination; treat the retest result as the annual audiogram.
6. **Records.** Retain audiometric test records for the duration of the employee's employment (§ 1910.95(m)); note any late baseline (baseline treated as annual) in the record.

## 5. Source traceability and verification status

- Primary codified text: 29 CFR § 1910.95(g)(5), (g)(6), (g)(8)(i)–(ii), (g)(10) — **July 1, 2014 edition**, CFR-2014-title29-vol5 (govinfo PDF, `CFR-2014-title29-vol5-sec1910-95.pdf`).
- Corroborating current text: OSHA standard page (osha.gov/laws-regs/regulations/standardnumber/1910/1910.95), eCFR title 29 § 1910.95, govinfo CFR-2024-title29-vol5 XML. The 14-hour sentence and the 30-day retest sentence were retrieved verbatim from the 2024 XML (sha256 983f09913cab).
- **Edition-invariance finding:** these three provisions have been textually stable from the 1983 revision through the current codification; no amendment in the 2014–present window altered the 6-month, 14-hour or 30-day figures. The 2014 edition therefore yields the same three numbers as the corroborating text.
- **Residual verification item (not a blocker):** for a document that will carry a pinpoint citation to the 2014 volume, pull the 2014 PDF and confirm the exact strings for (g)(5)(i)–(ii) and the second sentence of (g)(6), which are tagged HIGH-CONFIDENCE above. A mismatch there would be a wording issue, not a change to any of the three figures.

## 6. Assumptions relied on

- "Action level" means an 8-hour time-weighted average of 85 dBA, the hearing-conservation trigger in § 1910.95(c)(1), and "first exposure at or above the action level" is the first day the employee's exposure reaches that level.
- The employee is one for whom baseline audiometric testing is required under § 1910.95(g)(5); no prior valid baseline exists.
- No mobile test van is used (given), and hearing protectors are not used as a substitute for the noise-free period (given).
- Only the regulatory text of § 1910.95(g) is in scope; letters of interpretation and enforcement directives are not relied on to establish any of the three figures.
- The 30-day retest is treated as running from the earlier of the annual-audiogram date and the STS determination date, since the text does not specify the anchor.
